---
title: "Inside a project folder"
subtitle: "What every file and directory in a Flux project is, and which ones are yours"
---

A Flux project is a plain folder whose marker is `project.json`. Here is the canonical tree:

```
<project>/
├── project.json                 # the map: title, authors, documents, figures, references
├── manuscript/                  # YOURS — the prose (source of truth)
│   ├── main.qmd                 #   the main manuscript (Quarto markdown)
│   └── comments.json            #   margin-comment threads (a sidecar — never inside the .qmd)
├── plots/                       # YOURS — analysis output lands here, any structure you like
│   └── growth.{svg,fluxplot.json,recipe.json}   # a semantic plot + manifest + recipe
├── fig/                         # APP-MANAGED — the figure subsystem
│   ├── index.json               #   canvases + figures rollup
│   ├── canvases/<id>.json       #   the real compositions (figures → elements)
│   ├── captions/<id>.md         #   each figure's composed caption
│   ├── assets/                  #   Flux's imported copies of your plots
│   └── renders/                 #   derived static renders
├── slides/<deckId>/deck.json    # APP-MANAGED — one deck per folder (+ its assets/)
├── references/library.bib       # YOURS — the project's cited subset (BibTeX)
├── Context/                     # the agent layer
│   ├── Project/MISSION.qmd      #   the charter (co-owned: you have final say)
│   ├── NOTEBOOK.md              #   the principal agent's running memory
│   ├── RULES.md                 #   project rules (recurring feedback lands here)
│   ├── Transcripts/             #   captured agent-session transcripts
│   └── Dispatches/              #   worker briefs, logs, and results
├── styles/  assets/  exports/   # figure styles · media · compiled output (derived)
└── .meta/                       # tool state: journal, feedback ledger, locks, schemas
```

# Ownership at a glance

| Kind | Paths | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| **Yours — edit freely** | `manuscript/**.qmd`, `plots/`, `references/library.bib` | Source of truth. Edit in Flux, another editor, or a script — all equivalent. |
| **Co-owned with agents** | `Context/` | Mission and rules are shared; `NOTEBOOK.md` is the agent's memory — read and comment rather than rewrite. |
| **App-managed** | `fig/`, `slides/` | Readable JSON, but change it through the app or [`flux` commands](cli.qmd) so indexes and captions stay coherent. |
| **Derived** | `fig/renders/`, `exports/`, caches | Rebuildable output. Safe to ignore in backups and version control. |

# Notes on specific pieces

- **`project.json`** is a derived rollup — a fast map of the project, rebuilt from the real
  files (`flux reindex` refreshes it if a script edited things directly).
- **Comments live beside documents, never in them.** The main manuscript's threads are
  `manuscript/comments.json`; any other document's are `<name>.comments.json` next to it. Your
  `.qmd` prose stays clean.
- **`plots/` is a drop-zone with no imposed structure** — organize it however your analysis
  does. Flux only reads it, copying what you compose into `fig/assets/`. See
  [semantic plots](../concepts/semantic-plots.qmd) for the three-file contract.
- **`.meta/`** holds the operational machinery: `journal.ndjson` (every write: who/what/when),
  `feedback.ndjson` (your context-stamped notes to agents), advisory `locks/`, JSON `schema/`
  for every file type, and the live-bridge descriptor while the app is open.
- **`Context/`** is explained in full in [the collaboration system](../agents/collaboration.qmd).

For the philosophy behind the layout — source vs. derived, crash safety, live reload —
see [Projects are folders, files are the truth](../concepts/projects-and-files.qmd).
